subject: Litigation access v. arbitration — preservation & venue for MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Cara Liu <cara.liu@civitashealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@civitashealth.com, Michael Scott <mscott@jonesday.com>
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Civitas MSA redlines — court access for emergency relief

Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward but our procurement and legal teams asked that two points be clarified in the MSA and Order Form before we can route to PO:

1) Emergency relief: we need carveouts to the arbitration clause so our hospitals can seek preliminary injunctive relief in New York state or federal court to preserve urgent patient safety obligations.
2) Governing law: Civitas prefers New York law for the MSA but will consider reasonable compromise.

Attached are our redlines (Civitas_MSA_redline_v3.docx and OrderForm_Redline_20280518.pdf). Please confirm whether Redwood can accept a limited injunctive relief carveout and whether you will agree to New York as governing law or propose Redwood's shortlist. If you can send proposed language by EOD Monday that would help our procurement timeline (we're targeting signature by 5/25).

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call if easier.

Best,
Cara Liu
Senior Contracts Manager
Civitas Health

Subject: Re: Civitas MSA redlines — court access for emergency relief

Cara — thanks and thanks for the redlines. Quick read-through and initial reaction below; looping in Kimberly and Karthik for legal/negotiation stance.

High level: Redwood is generally willing to accept a narrow interim relief carveout for injunctive relief to prevent imminent patient-safety impact, provided the language is tightly limited (preserve rights only, no waiver of arbitration for the merits). We generally prefer to keep governing law in the state of our incorporation or a neutral US venue, but we can be flexible for large health systems.

Specific asks for legal:
- Draft proposed interim-relief carveout that preserves arbitration for merits but permits 'provisional remedies' (injunctive relief, attachment, etc.) in courts.
- Proposal for governing law and venue: suggest Redwood proposes 'State of Washington' or 'State of California' — happy to take Kimberly's recommendation.

I'll push procurement to stretch the internal timeline a bit (to 5/29) if we need counsel redline cycles.

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Civitas MSA redlines — court access for emergency relief

Vanessa / team — read Civitas' redlines. My recommended approach: accept a narrowly-tailored interim relief carveout but preserve arbitration for the merits. Language (draft below) has worked with other hospital systems and limits exposure. Feel free to pass the paragraph to Civitas.

Draft carveout paragraph (suggested):
"Notwithstanding the agreement to arbitrate disputes, either party may seek provisional or emergency relief (including temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions) in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve rights or prevent irreparable harm; such temporary relief shall not constitute a waiver of the obligation to arbitrate the dispute on the merits under this Agreement. Any such action for provisional relief shall be limited to injunctive or equivalent relief necessary to preserve the status quo pending arbitration."

Governing law / venue guidance: Redwood's corporate entity is incorporated in Delaware, with significant engineering ops in Washington state. To minimize negotiation friction I'd recommend proposing: Governing law: State of Washington; Venue for any court-based provisional relief: courts located in King County, Washington, or, at the election of the party seeking relief, the federal district court for the Western District of Washington. That gives Civitas a clear forum and keeps the merits in arbitration.

Additional notes:
- We should propose a mutual consent-to-service clause for provisional relief actions (so Civitas can effect service quickly if they go to court).
- Keep the carveout limited and add a sentence that parties will promptly move the merits to arbitration (to avoid tactical forum shopping).

I'll redline the MSA and send a tracked version in the next email.

Kimberly Park
Lead Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Cara Liu <cara.liu@civitashealth.com>

Cc: Michael Scott <mscott@jonesday.com>, procurement@civitashealth.com
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 08:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Civitas MSA redlines — court access for emergency relief

Vanessa / Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft language. A couple of clarifications from Civitas counsel (Michael copied):

1) Civitas' preference is NY law and NY courts for provisional relief because most hospital agreements for our group use New York for predictability; they will consider Washington if we provide an explicit carve that emergency relief in NY is permissible when servers/processes used for care are routed through our NY-based subsidiary.
2) They request that the carveout explicitly list 'injunctive relief, asset preservation, and provisional attachment' as permitted provisional remedies.

Michael — can you confirm whether the suggested mutual consent-to-service language would be acceptable? If so we'll re-run our redline vs Kimberly's paragraph and re-submit.

Cara
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
To: Cara Liu <cara.liu@civitashealth.com>, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Final position and next steps — Civitas MSA/Order Form

Thanks all. Quick summary and proposed next steps so procurement has a single path forward: 

1) Redwood accepts a limited provisional-relief carveout. Proposed paragraph (to be placed in Section 17, Dispute Resolution):
   - Limited carve: either party may seek provisional remedies (including injunctive relief, asset preservation, and attachment) in a court of competent jurisdiction to preserve rights or prevent irreparable harm; such remedies shall be without prejudice to the parties' obligation to arbitrate the substantive dispute. Any provisional relief granted shall not determine the merits of the dispute.
2) Governing law: Redwood proposes State of Washington as governing law for the Agreement.
3) Venue for provisional relief: King County, Washington courts or the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington, unless the parties agree in writing to New York in a narrowly-defined scenario tied to Civitas' NY subsidiary operations.
4) Mutual consent-to-service: include a clause that service for provisional relief may be effected by email to the parties' primary in-house counsel and by overnight courier to the registered agent.

Action items: 
- Kimberly to send tracked redline of the MSA with the carveout & consent-to-service text (Kim will attach final redline).
- Vanessa to confirm with Civitas procurement that 5/29 is an acceptable close window if one additional redline round is needed.
- Karthik and Marcus to prepare a brief escalation path if Civitas pushes for a full merits waiver of arbitration (we will not accept that).

Cara — can you confirm whether Civitas can accept Washington as Redwood's proposed governing law with the NY carve condition? If yes we will circulate the redline for a final look.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
